metaDesc: A day-by-day road trip from Sukhothai to Phrae, a quiet Lanna old town most tourists skip. Stop at Si Satchanalai en route — real routes, timings, food spots, and prices.

ogTitle: Sukhothai–Phrae 3 Days 2 Nights: One Road, Two Old Towns
ogDesc: Drive north from Sukhothai to Phrae — teak city, mor hom indigo cloth, and a genuinely unhurried old town. Stop at Si Satchanalai on the way. Day-by-day plan.
intro: Sukhothai and Phrae sit on the same road north — and that connection gets overlooked far too often. Drive Highway 101 through Si Satchanalai and Den Chai, and you land in Phrae: a city built on teak, known for indigo-dyed cloth, and still genuinely quiet. This plan gives you half a day in Sukhothai's ruins, a midway stop at Si Satchanalai, then two easy days in Phrae without rushing — temples, a century-old mansion district, and the kind of northern food that doesn't cost much.

blocks.html: Sukhothai to Phrae is about 159 km — roughly 2.5 hours driving straight through. The real draw is what's along the way, especially Si Satchanalai Historical Park, which sits right on Highway 101. You dip in, then continue through Den Chai into Phrae without retracing a single kilometer.

These two cities tell stories from different eras that actually complement each other well. Sukhothai was the capital of the first major Thai kingdom; Phrae was a prosperous Lanna city that grew wealthy on teak timber, leaving behind mansion estates and old wooden temples. Most people visit Sukhothai and head straight home, even though Phrae is only two hours further north. It's still one of the least-crowded historic towns in northern Thailand — you can walk the old city streets without fighting for space or a decent photo.

items: One road, no backtracking — Highway 101 runs from Sukhothai through Si Satchanalai, Den Chai, and straight into Phrae.
Two completely different atmospheres — Sukhothai is open-air ruins in the plains; Phrae is a living Lanna town with teak architecture.
Phrae is still genuinely quiet — fewer tourists means walkable streets, affordable food, and lodging that doesn't need booking weeks ahead.

blocks.title: Getting there: you need a car
blocks.html: This route is best driven — either your own vehicle or a rental. There's no direct public transport between Sukhothai and Phrae; the alternative is connecting through Phitsanulok, which takes most of a day. If you're flying in, land at Phitsanulok and rent a car there, or rent from Sukhothai city.

blocks.text: Day 1 · Sukhothai in the morning, then drive to Phrae

items.activity: Breakfast in Sukhothai town before heading out
items.note: The morning market has khao bip and Sukhothai noodles — worth eating here before you leave.

items.activity: Walk the inner zone of Sukhothai Historical Park — Wat Mahathat and Wat Si Chum
items.note: Morning light is cooler and softer. You can walk or rent a bicycle. Entry for Thais is 20 THB per zone (foreigners 200 THB for the inner zone).

items.activity: Leave Sukhothai, take Highway 101 north toward Si Satchanalai
items.note: About 55 km — roughly 1 hour.

items.activity: Explore Si Satchanalai Historical Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site alongside Sukhothai
items.note: Wat Chang Lom and Wat Chedi Chet Thaew are the standouts. Far fewer visitors than Sukhothai.

items.activity: Lunch near Sawankhalok / Si Satchanalai before continuing north
items.note: Several noodle shops and local eateries along the highway.

items.activity: Continue on 101 through Den Chai into Phrae city
items.note: Around 100 km, about 1.5 hours. The road rolls through low hills with decent scenery.

items.activity: Check in to your Phrae accommodation, then head out to walk the old town
items.note: Staying inside or near the old city wall puts temples, mansions, and cafés within easy walking distance.

items.activity: Stroll around Pratu Chai (the old town gate) and the city wall — good light for photos
items.note: Evening street food appears around the gate on most days; occasionally a walking street sets up here.

blocks.text: Day 2 · Full day in Phrae's old town — temples, mansions, mor hom

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Phrae Old Town + Wat Phrathat Cho Hae

items.activity: Breakfast: Phrae-style khanom jeen nam sai (clear pork broth noodles)
items.note: A local specialty — light, clear pork bone broth with rice noodles. Easy to find at morning shops in town.

items.activity: Visit Wat Phrabat Ming Mueang Woravihan, Phrae's principal temple
items.note: Houses Phra Phuttha Kosai Sirichi Maha Sakayamuni and a small Lanna art museum.

items.activity: Tour Khum Chao Luang and Baan Wongburi — century-old teak mansions
items.note: Khum Chao Luang blends Thai and European architecture; Baan Wongburi is the well-known pink house.

items.activity: Lunch at a northern Thai restaurant — try khao soi or nam ngiao
items.note: Several long-running khao soi spots in Phrae town. Expect to pay around 40–60 THB a bowl.

items.activity: Visit Ban Thung Hong, Phrae's indigo cloth weaving village
items.note: Less than 10 km from town. Watch the natural dyeing process and pick up mor hom shirts as souvenirs.

items.activity: Head up to Wat Phrathat Cho Hae, Phrae's sacred hilltop chedi
items.note: About 9 km from town. Locals will tell you: if you come to Phrae, you pay respects at Cho Hae.

items.activity: Find a teak-house café for an afternoon break — Phrae has a good few
items.note: Specialty coffee in old wooden shophouses around the town center. Drinks run about 45–70 THB.

items.activity: Dinner in town, then a quiet evening walk
items.note: Phrae at night is genuinely calm — a good stroll after eating.

blocks.text: Day 3 · Off-the-radar spots before heading home

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Phae Mueang Phi + temple stop before driving back

items.activity: Breakfast and check out
items.note: Pack up and settle the bill — today is a sightseeing loop before you leave.

items.activity: Visit Phae Mueang Phi Forest Park — unusual eroded earth pillars
items.note: A natural formation of soil and rock shaped by erosion. Follow the walkway through; morning is cooler and better lit.

items.activity: Stop at Wat Chom Sawan — the only Burmese Bagan-style building in Phrae
items.note: A teak building over a century old, now a registered historic monument.

items.activity: Lunch in Phrae town, last chance to pick up mor hom souvenirs
items.note: If you haven't bought enough indigo cloth yet, town shops are your last stop before the drive.

items.activity: Head out — return to Sukhothai the same way, or continue north to Nan or Lampang
items.note: Phrae is a northern crossroads: Nan is about 2 hours east, Lampang about 1.5 hours west.

blocks.text: Food you shouldn't miss along this route

items: Khao bip / Sukhothai noodles — eat these in Sukhothai before you leave. Light, slightly sweet broth with sliced long beans.
Phrae khanom jeen nam sai — the city's breakfast staple, rice noodles in a clear pork bone broth with a soft, rounded flavor.
Khao soi and nam ngiao — northern Thai classics that Phrae does well, at very reasonable prices.
Teak-house cafés in Phrae — specialty coffee in old wooden buildings, quiet atmosphere, good for a slow afternoon.

blocks.title: Adjusting the plan
blocks.html: Only have 2 days? Drop Day 3 and do Phae Mueang Phi as a morning stop before driving back. If you have more time, Phrae connects naturally to Nan — they're on the same road and Nan is worth a trip in its own right.

This plan is built around 2 nights in Phrae, since that's the destination you want to spend proper time in. If you'd rather not rush Sukhothai on the first morning, add one night there before driving north — you'll arrive in Phrae more relaxed. Either way, stay in or close to the old walled city in both towns; that's where the temples, mansions, and food are, and you won't need to move the car much.

items.name: Stay inside Phrae old town
items.blurb: Walk to Pratu Chai, Wat Phrabat, Khum Chao Luang, and cafés without needing the car. Best for unhurried exploring.

items.name: One night in Sukhothai first
items.blurb: Good option if you want a full morning at the historical park before driving north to Phrae the next day.

faq.q: How far is Sukhothai from Phrae, and how long does it take?
faq.a: About 159 km — roughly 2.5 hours driving straight through on Highway 101 via Si Satchanalai and Den Chai. If you stop at Si Satchanalai along the way, plan for a full, unhurried day.

faq.q: Is there direct public transport from Sukhothai to Phrae?
faq.a: No direct service. The usual workaround is connecting through Phitsanulok, which takes most of the day. This route is really built for self-drive or a rental car.

faq.q: What is there to do in Phrae, and how many days do you need?
faq.a: In the old city: Pratu Chai, Wat Phrabat Ming Mueang, Khum Chao Luang, and Baan Wongburi. Outside town: Wat Phrathat Cho Hae, Ban Thung Hong for mor hom cloth, and Phae Mueang Phi. One full day covers the old city; two days lets you add the out-of-town spots comfortably.

faq.q: What should I stop at between Sukhothai and Phrae?
faq.a: Si Satchanalai Historical Park sits right on Highway 101 — a UNESCO World Heritage site shared with Sukhothai, with far fewer visitors. It makes a natural halfway stop without any detour.

faq.q: What should I buy as a souvenir from Phrae?
faq.a: Mor hom — indigo-dyed cloth and shirts from Ban Thung Hong village, less than 10 km from the city center. You can watch the natural dyeing process and buy directly from the community.
